analysis.title: The Wolfe Power Trip
key_insights: Wolfe lowers its utilities sentiment meter one notch to 3. IPPs were hit as the AI trade came under pressure, first from the CRWV selloff, then continued pressure after META earnings, with SPCX earnings giving only brief relief.
Midterm elections are approaching and political rhetoric around data centers remains difficult for the group.
Wolfe says stock-specific fundamentals did not change much to the negative. It cites improvement from CEG's GOOGL/AMZN deals and FERC rejecting PJM's IRAS proposal.
Wolfe has a relative preference for the PJM names, CEG first and TLN second, going into Q3 earnings.

Wolfe expects softer 2027 guidance for NRG. VST is waiting on the Cogentrix close and may not give a 2028 outlook. TLN's outlook through 2029 should be mostly in line. CEG's guidance refresh comes with Q4.

IPP two-year forward FCF yield is near the highest since the AI boom began in early 2024. The IPP average is 11% today versus a 9% average since the AI trade began and 12% since CEG began trading in February 2022. The 10-year average is 16.0%.
By name, TLN's FCF yield is above its history, NRG is just above its long-term average, CEG is in line with its 5-year average, and VST is still well below its average.
Wolfe argues it is a misconception that IPPs hit peak earnings in 2027-2028, because data center deals are ramping, commodity curves are not in backwardation, and excess FCF goes to buybacks.
Two-year forward EV/EBITDA for IPPs briefly hit the 15-year average of 7.8x, rebounded, then retraced most of the way. It is 8.0x as of 10/23/26.

IPP FCF yields exclude much of the contracted upside. CEG's 2027 FCF omits the AMZN/GOOGL nuclear deals (3.2 GW), TLN only includes the first 360 MW of the Susquehanna contract (ramping to 1,920 MW), and VST only includes half of the 2.2 GW META nuclear PPA and almost none of the 1.2 GW AMZN Comanche Peak PPA.

IPPs were about 80% correlated with an equal-weighted AI basket in 2025, decoupled in 2026 on the most recent leg higher, then recoupled in the latest drawdown. Wolfe views IPP businesses as increasingly defensive even though the stocks are not trading that way.
FERC largely denied PJM's IRAS proposal on 10/9, accepting only the large load registry. PJM must file compliance on the registry by 11/8.

FERC partially accepted PJM's reliability backstop procurement (RBP) on 9/29 but flagged cost allocation, Transmission Owner Exit rules and LSE collateral requirements. PJM plans to file revisions by 10/29, and FERC then has 60 days. Procurement is planned for March 2027 with results on May 3, 2027.

The PJM 2028/2029 capacity auction cleared at the $325/MW-day cap, 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement. It would have priced at $555/MW-day uncapped. The 2029/2030 auction runs in December 2026 with results on 12/22 and is the last with the collar.
State comments on PJM long-term capacity reform (OPSI, PUCO) supported voluntary hedging and long-term capacity products, which Wolfe views as better than feared.
VST's $4.0B Cogentrix acquisition (5.5 GW) has FERC and several state approvals. DoJ approval remains, with close expected in late 2026.
Wolfe's market power prices are above its own 2027 PJM West assumption (market $70.60 vs Wolfe $65.32, 5.2% gap). Nymex gas is $2.98 for 2026 against Wolfe's $3.34.

market_movers.rationale: Wolfe has a relative preference for CEG among PJM names. The AMZN/GOOGL deals are not yet captured in 2027 FCF, and the guidance refresh comes with Q4.
Wolfe ranks TLN second among PJM names. Its FCF yield is above history and the Susquehanna contract is only partly in estimates. Outlook through 2029 should be mostly in line.
Wolfe expects softer 2027 guidance. NRG is the cheapest IPP on FCF yield at 15.4% for 2026.
VST is waiting on the Cogentrix close and may not give a 2028 outlook. Its FCF yield is still well below its own average.

sector_views.rationale: Sentiment meter lowered to 3 on AI trade pressure. Valuation has improved with FCF yields near AI-era highs. Preference is for PJM names CEG and TLN.

earnings_insights: Wolfe expects softer 2027 guidance from NRG, with no figure given.
VST may not give a 2028 outlook because the Cogentrix deal has not closed.
TLN's outlook through 2029 should be mostly in line with current estimates.
CEG's guidance refresh will come with Q4. Wolfe sees its recent commercial success as a strong discussion point.
CEG EPS estimates, Wolfe vs consensus: 2026 $12.36 vs $12.04, 2027 $13.42 vs $13.33, 2028 $16.93 vs $16.92. These are Wolfe estimates and consensus figures, not reported results.

EBITDA estimates, Wolfe vs consensus: NRG 2026 $5,447M vs $5,489M, 2027 $5,800M vs $5,968M. TLN 2026 $2,180M vs $2,141M, 2027 $2,728M vs $2,705M. VST 2026 $7,291M vs $7,292M, 2027 $7,945M vs $8,057M. All are estimates.
PEG EPS, Wolfe vs consensus: 2026 $4.37 vs $4.38, 2027 $4.66 vs $4.64, 2028 $5.00 vs $5.00. All are estimates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The auction cleared at the cap and would have priced at $555/MW-day uncapped ($777 in ComEd), 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement.
This is close to the 15-year average of 7.8x.
The average is 12% since CEG began trading and 9% since the AI trade began. The 10-year average is 16.0%.
This is about 10.6% below Wolfe's assumption of $3.34, which is a headwind for gas-linked estimates.
The market price is 5.2% above Wolfe's $65.32 assumption.

risk_factors: Continued pressure on the AI trade, which is dragging on the IPPs.
Political rhetoric around data centers ahead of the midterm elections.
Regulatory risk in PJM, including the RBP cost allocation, co-location filings and capacity market reform.
Texas data center affordability measures and the SB6 rulemaking.
Softer 2027 guidance at NRG and no 2028 outlook at VST.
charts_described: Exhibit 7 plots IPP average two-year forward MTM EV/EBITDA against its 15-year average. The current reading is 8.0x as of 10/23/26 versus the average of 7.8x.
vol_and_positioning: The IPPs are trading with the AI basket again. Funds had rotated from higher-beta AI names back into IPPs before the latest drawdown.
geopolitical: The White House/PJM Governors' Statement of Principles in January 2026 pushed IPPs into regulatory uncertainty.
The U.S./Japan $66B investment in 18.7 GW of new gas generation is early stage.
The U.S./South Korea $22B investment in a 6.5 GW gas project in Texas (Project Star) was announced in early October.
Energy Secretary Wright urged FERC to speed data center grid connection reviews.

tension_points.bull_case: FCF yields are near AI-era highs and close to the average since CEG began trading. Contracted cash flows ramp into the early 2030s and are not fully in estimates. Wolfe calls peak-earnings fears in 2027-2028 a misconception.
tension_points.bear_case: IPPs have recoupled with the AI basket during the drawdown. Political rhetoric on data centers is rising before the midterms, and the yield remains well below the 16.0% 10-year average.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued AI trade weakness and adverse regulatory outcomes in PJM, including the FERC rulings on RBP cost allocation and co-location.

theme_stances.key_argument: IPP FCF yields are higher than recent history and not far from long-term averages, while the businesses are stronger than before.
theme_stances.evidence: these businesses are vastly better than they were even a few years ago

theme_stances.key_argument: The IPPs recoupled with the AI trade during the latest drawdown even though their cash flows are increasingly defensive.
theme_stances.evidence: the IPPs started to recouple with the AI trade
